evidence: src/business/services/LendingService.ts: constructor injects `BookGateway`, `MemberGateway`, `LoanGateway` and maps records into `Book`, `Member`, `Loan` domain models (e.g. `loadBook`, `new Member(...)`).
src/business/services/LoanHistoryService.ts: constructor injects `PrismaService` and `eventsOf` calls `this.db.loanEvent.findMany` directly, with no gateway or domain model.
src/business/services/LoanHistoryService.ts: `note()` runs `const db = new PrismaClient();` and so ignores the injected `this.db`.
Duplicated ID-generation rule: LendingService `private sequence = 0; ... `loan-${this.sequence}`` vs LoanHistoryService `private counter = 0; ... `evt-${this.counter}``.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files cover a related area: lending, returning and loan history. The problem is how they get to data. LendingService.ts always goes through injected gateways (BookGateway, MemberGateway, LoanGateway) and turns records into domain models (Book, Member, Loan). LoanHistoryService.ts drops that approach and works with Prisma directly. Inside note() it even ignores its own injected `db: PrismaService` and creates a new `PrismaClient()`, while eventsOf() uses the injected `this.db`. So the file does not use its own injected dependency consistently. Separately, both services create IDs with their own private in-memory counter (`loan-${this.sequence}` and `evt-${this.counter}`). This rule appears twice instead of living in one place, and the counters are not safe across instances. Import direction is out of scope and was not judged. This failure is about inconsistent abstractions and the bypass.

violations.message: note() creates `new PrismaClient()` and so bypasses the injected `PrismaService` (`this.db`), which eventsOf() does use. The file is inconsistent with its own injected dependency.

Uses the Prisma client directly for loanEvent and returns plain objects, while the rest of the module goes through gateways (BookGateway/LoanGateway/MemberGateway) and domain models. The module's data-access abstraction is used inconsistently.

Has its own in-memory ID counter (`private sequence`, `loan-${this.sequence}`), and LoanHistoryService repeats the same pattern (`private counter`, `evt-${this.counter}`). The ID-generation rule should live in one place.
